lines.trans: This inspector refused to drink our wine!
Chef, what are we to do now?
Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!
Do you want to add alcohol to food?
Louis, prepare a dessert with cognac for him!
How many spoonfuls of cognac to add to the cream?
Pour from the heart, do not spare cognac!
And how to deal with hot dishes?
We will generously pour dry wine into the meat.
The inspector will definitely taste strong alcohol.
He will not notice anything in the sauce!
Chef, this is a very daring and dangerous plan.
At least our restaurant will be saved, work!

words.gloss: at least, but on other hand

Chef, what are we to do now?
Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!

words.gloss: at least, but on other hand

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'alcohol' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you planning to drink alcohol?

examples.text: А если он откажется от алкоголя?
examples.trans: And what if he refuses alcohol?

examples.text: Вы хотите добавить алкоголь в еду?
examples.trans: Do you want to add alcohol to food?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Serve the hot dishes.
This is the restaurant's signature dish.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'wine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is very good wine.
A glass of red wine.
I got Chilean wine.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'taste', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('taste, preference') (не в моём вкусе = not my type) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You are not my type.
She has good taste.

examples.text: Я бы рад вам помочь. Но вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: I would be glad to help you. But unfortunately you are not my type.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What are you doing?
I'm making dinner.
Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'daring', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: That was a daring plan.

examples.text: Шеф, это очень дерзкий и опасный план.
examples.trans: Chef, this is a very daring and dangerous plan.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'dessert' (from 'desservir', to clear the table).

examples.trans: This is a dessert.
To order dessert.
Delicious desserts.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to add', forming an aspectual pair with 'добавлять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to append') (to say in addition) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я просто хотел добавить яркий аромат.
examples.trans: I simply wanted to add a vivid aroma.

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'soul', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('standing over someone') (colloquial idiom) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Why are you hovering over me?
A kind soul.

examples.text: У меня на душе сильная тревога.
examples.trans: I have a strong anxiety in my soul.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'food', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Oh, bad food?

examples.text: В этом ресторане всегда свежая еда.
examples.trans: There is always fresh food in this restaurant.
Oh no, bad food? Does your stomach hurt?

meanings.en: to spare, grudge; to regret, pity
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to pity'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Шеф не жалеет специй для соуса.
examples.trans: The chef does not spare spices for the sauce.

examples.text: Лей от души, коньяка не жалей!
examples.trans: Pour from the heart, do not spare cognac!

examples.text: Я очень сильно жалею о своей глупости.
examples.trans: I very deeply regret my foolishness.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.trans: But you've still got some.
But I know.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to notice', forming an aspectual pair with 'замечать'.

examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.
And what if someone notices me?

зато.gloss: but on the other hand, to make up for it

meanings.en: but on the other hand, at least
meanings.note: introduces a compensating positive fact

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.
The flat is small, but at least it's in the centre.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Сейчас зато аппетит нагуляем.
examples.trans: No big deal. At least we'll walk up an appetite now.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: From Latin 'inspector' (observer, overseer, from 'inspicere', to look into).

examples.trans: The inspector checked the restaurant kitchen.
Inspectors look for violations.

examples.text: Инспекторы ищут нарушения только ради денег.
examples.trans: Inspectors look for violations only for money.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?
As you all know...
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: genitive also 'коньяку' (some cognac)

examples.trans: He drinks French cognac.
The cognac is very expensive.
And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cream', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Кондитер взбил нежный крем для торта.
examples.trans: The pastry chef whipped delicate cream for the cake.

examples.text: Сколько ложек коньяка добавить в крем?
examples.trans: How many spoonfuls of cognac to add to the cream?
Louis, I finished whipping the cream.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'strong', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Your grip is strong.
He has strong health.

examples.text: Рука у тебя крепкая, как у деда.
examples.trans: Your grip is strong, just like your grandfather's.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to pour'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Pour oil into the frying pan.

examples.text: Лей от души, коньяка не жалей!
examples.trans: Pour from the heart, do not spare cognac!

meanings.note: чайная ложка = teaspoon, столовая ложка = tablespoon

examples.trans: Give me a spoon, please.
He eats soup with a spoon.
And take his eye out with a spoon.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'meat', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Where do you get your meat?
Very tasty meat!

examples.text: И мой тоже готов! А ты где мясо берёшь?
examples.trans: And mine is ready too! Where do you get your meat?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'кормить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to feed'.

examples.trans: The cook fed the guests deliciously.

examples.text: Раз не можем напоить, мы его накормим!
examples.trans: Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!

examples.text: Мы накормим его вкусным горячим обедом.
examples.trans: We will feed him a delicious hot lunch.

meanings.note: налей мне чаю = pour me some tea; налей мужу = pour your husband a drink

examples.trans: Pour me some tea.
I've poured you some water.
Nina, pour your husband a drink. We've got something to celebrate!

напоить.gloss: to give to drink, water, intoxicate

meanings.en: to give drink to, hydrate, intoxicate
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'поить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give to drink'.

examples.trans: They decided to give the guest tea to drink.

examples.text: Раз не можем напоить, мы его накормим!
examples.trans: Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I don't know anything.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dangerous').

examples.trans: I have many dangerous friends.
This is a very dangerous job.

examples.text: У меня много опасных друзей. А иначе я позвоню ребятам.
examples.trans: I have many dangerous friends. Otherwise I'll call the guys.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'from' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('of') (тошнит от = sick of) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: A letter from Mum.
I'm tired of work.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: intransitive reflexive verb with infinitive or от + genitive

examples.trans: He refused to sign the report.
She declined the offered money.
Really? Did he refuse to sign it?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to drink', forming an aspectual pair with 'выпить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.trans: I'm drinking tea.
He doesn't drink.

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.
What is our plan?

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

поступить.gloss: to enter, to get into (a university); to act

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ступить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to enter', forming an aspectual pair with 'поступать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to act, to behave') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Yulia needs to get into university.
He got into university.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чувствовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to feel'.

examples.trans: The guest smelled the pleasant aroma of the dish.

examples.text: Инспектор точно почувствует вкус крепкого алкоголя.
examples.trans: The inspector will definitely taste strong alcohol.

examples.text: Поверь мне, никто не почувствует разницу!
examples.trans: Believe me, nobody will feel the difference!

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.trans: I made a cake.
Mum cooked a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: 'один раз' = once, 'два раза' = twice

examples.trans: Just once.
Say it once more.
What do you mean, once?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.
Secondary conversational sense ('what a lot of!') (in exclamations) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So much gum!
How much is it?
So much gum! Cool!

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to save', forming an aspectual pair with 'спасать'.

examples.trans: I saved the monastery!
He rescued the cat.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'dry', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: The branch is dry!

examples.text: Нам нужны сухие дрова для костра.
examples.trans: We need dry firewood for the campfire.
The branch is dry! Look, our scout.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Lyolya will definitely come!

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'generously'.

examples.trans: The cook generously sprinkled the dish with herbs.

examples.text: В мясо мы щедро нальём сухое вино.
examples.trans: We will generously pour dry wine into the meat.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
